To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the actin cytokkeleton is involved in cell volume regulation by controlling the activation of ion channels, and that the actin-binding protein ABP-280 is involved in the regulation of the cell volume response by modulating the actin cytoplasmic network.

the hypotonic stress-induced RVD in human melanoma A375 cells, which is mediated by a Ca2+-activated K+ channel, is regulated by a dynamic process of actin filament reorganization, which in turn targets the plasma membrane and ion channels.

the hypotonic shock-initiated cell volume regulatory decrease in human melanoma A375 cells is mediated by a regulatory "sensing" mechanism, which is dependent on the actin-binding protein ABP-280 and its ability to control actin filament organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the mechanisms by which the cell volume regulatory system controls the actin cytokeleton, and the identification of the effector mechanism(s) which target the cell volume regulatory ion channels.
the role of dynamic changes in actin cytoskeletal organization in cell volume regulation.
elucidating the role of actin filament dynamics in the control of cell volume and ion channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the actin cyto- skeleton, as an integral part of the cell, is a key component in the control of cell volume, and that the actin filament network is a dynamic structure, which is able to respond to cell volume regulatory stimuli and to effect signals to control membrane function, including the activity of ion channels.
actin filament organization plays a role in the control of cell volume and ion channels.
the actin cyto-skeleton is an integral part of the regulatory network controlling cell volume and ion transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the actin cyto-skeleton is a key component of the cell volume regulatory response, which may be involved in the regulation of cell volume through its ability to sense changes in intracellular ion concentration and to respond with changes in its own organization, thus affecting the function of ion channel proteins.

the actin cyto-skeleton may be involved in cell volume regulation by sensing changes in the intracytoplasmic water-salt homeo-stasis and by transmitting the signal to membrane-associated effector mechanisms controlling ion channel activity and thus cell volume.
actin filaments, as a result of changes in their gel properties, are involved in the control of cell volume by modulating the activity of ion channels and other transport mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the actin cyoskeleton is not only a "structural" network, but also a "dynamic" and "functional" network, which is involved, through the modulation of its gel properties, in the control of ion channel activity and thus cell volume.
the cytoskeleton may be involved in sensing changes in intracellular water-saline homeostasis and in turn, in the regulation of cell volume and ion channels.
actin filament organization is an important effector mechanism in ion channel regulation and thus cell volume.
